title.narrative: Strenghtening womens rights and womens participation in North Macedonia (Ktk)
Stärka kvinnors rättigheter och kvinnors deltagande i Nordmakedonien (Ktk)

description.narrative:
Kvinna till Kvinna har ansökt om finansiering på 18 500 000 SEK för att genomföra projektet "Strenghtening womens rights and womens participation in North Macedonia" under perioden 2020-2023.
Det övergripande målet för projektet är att Kvinna till Kvinna och dess lokala partnerorganisationer ska påverka politik och praxis när det gäller könsbaserat våld, agendan för kvinnor, fred och säkerhet (WPS-agendan) och kvinnors ekonomiska befogenheter i Nordmakedonien.
Projektet presenterar fyra delmål - ett för vart och ett av de tre tematiska områdena och ett fjärde som täcker alla områden:
1. Partnerorganisationer bidrar till bättre tillgång till rättslig prövning för rättighetsbärare och rättsstatsprinciper genom policy- och attitydförändringar avseende genusbaserat våld. 2. Partnerorganisationer skapar förutsättningar för kvinnor och flickor att delta fullt och effektivt i utvecklingen av ett jämlikt och demokratiskt samhälle och för genomförandet av agendan för kvinnor, fred och säkerhet (WPS-agendan). 3. Organisationer som nås inom projektet bidrar till förändringar i politik och praxis när det gäller kvinnors ekonomiska bemyndigande. 4. Ett mer levande civilsamhälle genom ökad hållbarhet för organisationer som fokuserar på kvinnors rättigheter.
Projektet kommer att genomföras av Kvinna till Kvinna i samarbete med relevanta partnerorganisationer.
Sida är den enda givaren som har blivit tillfrågad om att ge stöd till denna insats.

Kvinna till kvinna has applied to the Embassy of Sweden for funding of 18,5 MSEK to carry out the project "Strenghtening womens rights and womens participation in North Macedonia" during the period 2020-2023.
The overall objective of the project is that Kvinna till Kvinna and partner organisations will influence policy and practice regarding gender-based violence, the women peace and security agenda and women’s economic empowerment in North Macedonia.
The project presents four intermediate objectives - one for each of the three thematic areas and a fourth covering all areas:
1. Partner organisations contribute to better access to justice for rights holders and rule of law through policy and attitude changes regarding GBV. 2. Partner organisations create conditions for women and girls to participate fully and effectively in the development of an equal and democratic society, and towards the implementation of the women, peace and security agenda. 3. Organisations reached within the program contribute to changes in policy and practice regarding women’s economic empowerment. 4. A more vibrant civil society through increased sustainability of women’s rights organisations.
The project will be implemented by Kvinna till Kvinna in collaboration with relevant partner organisations.
Sida is the only donor invited by Kvinna till kvinna for support of this intervention.

The overall objective of the project was that Kvinna till Kvinna and local partner organisations influenced policy and practice regarding gender-based violence, the women peace and security agenda and women's economic empowerment in North Macedonia. By working towards this objective, the project aimed to contribute to the long-term outcome that: North Macedonia is a democratic society where women rights and participation is secured, with a vibrant and pluralistic civil society. The project presents four intermediate objectives - one for each of the three thematic areas and a fourth covering all areas.
Programme objective was that Kvinna till Kvinna and partner organizations influence policy and practice regarding gender-based violence, the women, peace and security agenda, and women economic empowerment in North Macedonia.
The four intermediate objectives were:
- Partner organizations contribute to better access to justice for rights holders and rule of law through policy and attitude changes regarding Gender Based Violence (GBV). - Partner organizations create conditions for women and girls to participate fully and effectively in the development of an equal and democratic society, and towards the implementation of the women, peace, and security agenda. - Organizations reached within the program contribute to changes in policy and practice regarding women economic empowerment. - A more vibrant civil society through increased sustainability of women rights organizations.
Under the area of women, peace and security focus was placed on increasing participation of women in decision-making at national and local level, on promoting feminist peace in different fora, both local, national and international; providing safe spaces for Women Human Right Defenders (WHRDs) and Women CSOs to discuss and plan strategies and advocacy actions related to safety and security for WHRDs while countering the anti-gender movement. The work on women participation in policy-and decision-making, was especially implemented at local levels.
Through the support to and cooperation with partner organisations, Kvinna till Kvinna used advocacy to influence relevant stakeholders at local, national and international level. Apart from advocacy, the main methods that Kvinna till Kvinna used to reach the programme goals were financial and political support to women rights organisations, capacity development, networking, communication and outreach. The target groups of the intervention were manifold - both at local and national levels as well as targeting the public. For instance, the project aimed to have an influence on local municipalities, mayors and civil society organisations, as well as national government, ministries and intersectoral working groups.
The project was Agreed for implementing period 1st December 2020 to 31st December 2023, and cost-extended until 30 September 2024. In continuity and based on the findings and recommendations of the external project evaluation, second Amendment to the Agreement was signed agreeing on cost-extension for extended project implementation period until 31st March 2025.Throughout the cost-extension period the vital and necessary support to partner organizations was continued.
The total project budget for the period 1st December 2020 - 31st March 2025 was 27 mSEK.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
In the frames of the project a total number of 10 partner organizations including : National Network to End Violence Against Women and Domestic Violence (the National Network); Glasen Tekstilec; Association for Advancement of Gender Equality Akcija Zdruzenska; Association for Emancipation, Solidarity and Equality of Women (ESE); HERA Health Education and Research Association; Organization of Women Sveti Nikole (OWMSVN); Association of Persons with Cerebral Palsy and other Disabilities (APCPOD); EcHO - Educational Humanitarian Organization; Organization Zena Delchevo; Womens Forum Tetovo; and 13 grassroots organizations were supported.
The supported organizations further reached hundreds of duty bearers and stakeholders at all levels of governments; provided services and awareness raising to rights holders across the country; and targeted the entire population with public campaigns.
Some key results include:
- Allocation of municipal funds to support the establishment of counselling centres for women victims of violence by three municipalities (Kavadarci, Bitola and Tetovo), following a joint advocacy by the National Network and their subgrantees. These centers present a significant improvement in the access to services for survivors of gender-based violence in these areas, which previously were lacking services.
- The National Network and ESE successfully participated in drafting amendments to align the Criminal Code with the Istanbul Convention. In 2023, these amendments were adopted, enhancing victim protection by criminalizing stalking, sexual harassment, and female genital mutilation, while also updating the definitions of GBV, femicide, and rape, thus advancing alignment with the Istanbul Convention and international human rights standards.
- EcHO - Shtip coordinated multi-sectoral teams across several municipalities, training representatives of the police, judiciary, social work centres, health services, and local self-government. Following the multi-sectoral approach and EcHOs persistent advocacy, landmark rulings were achieved in two tragic femicide cases, where the courts imposed the strictest possible sentence: life imprisonment for both perpetrators, setting an important legal precedent in the fight against GBV.
- Glasen Textilec monitored 26 court cases related to labor rights violations, a number of which were successfully resolved in favor of the women workers, including the landmark Soni TEX Kavadarci case, where 69 textile workers from Kavadarci filed a lawsuit over unpaid wages and overtime. With Glasen Tekstilecs support, the case gained media attention and was appealed, and in March 2024, the Appellate Court overturned the initial ruling, marking a significant win for women workers. This case exposed systemic shortcomings within the judiciary and labor inspection systems, but thanks to Glasen Tekstilec's dedicated engagement, it ultimately led to a precedent-setting ruling and financial compensation for the affected workers. Moreover, Glasen Textilec submitted three strategic cases of pregnancy-based discrimination to the Commission for Prevention and Protection against Discrimination. All three were successfully resolved in favor of the women workers, and the case of Magdalena Stojmanovikj became the first officially confirmed case of gender-based discrimination in the country, setting an important precedent and encouraging other women to come forward and report violations.
- Working jointly, Glasen Tekstilec and APCPOD organized awareness-raising sessions for over 100 women and men with disabilities, educating them about their labor rights and the process for reporting violations.
- Meanwhile HERA were successful in supporting Roma women and girls in accessing the labor market, with the number of Roma women registered as active job seekers with the Employment Agency increased from 64 in 2023 to 108 in 2024. Participation in employment measures outlined in the National Operational Plan for Employment rose from 17 Roma women in 2023 to 71 in 2024, leading to 25 Roma women being employed in 2025, compared to 1 in 2023.
- Through their sub-granting scheme and engagement at the local level, Akcija Zdruzenska and their sub-grantees established the Womens Circle networks, currently spanning 64 villages across 21 municipalities, with more than 500 women actively engaged. Local engagement further resulted in notable change in confidence and increase of initiatives among local women, and more than 100 advocacy proposals presented by women were accepted by local institutions. Thanks to the capacity development provided throughout the programme, supported organizations have enhanced financial monitoring, budgeting, and operational efficiency. Supported organizations have also developed strategic communication and digital resilience.
Throughout the programme, the Kvinna till Kvinna Skopje office have coordinated with and advocated towards several embassies, facilitating meetings with partner organizations and opportunities for fundraising.
Kvinna till Kvinna also cooperated with other Sida partners including EKO Svest, State Statistical Office, We Effect, Olof Palme Center/SIER, and engaged with other partners and stakeholders such as the Heinrich Böll Foundation, EIGE, Council of Europe, TACSO, Impact Foundation, Association of Business Women.
More specifically in 2023, Kvinna till Kvinna and Olof Palme Center facilitated a joint meeting between partners - Helsinki Committee for Human Rights, Reactor and Coalition Margins and the Union of Industry, Energy and Mining SIER on the Labor Law, where participants exchanged expertise, including on shared parental leave.
The project was implemented in a globally worsening context with ongoing war in Ukraine, strengthening global anti-gender movement which reflected with rising anti-gender sentiment in the country that was supported by the governing conservative political majority at central and local level. The Government in general deprioritized gender equality and cooperation with Women CSO's, and even turned the "blind eye" to the cases of social media attacks against women human rights defenders and gender equality advocates.
The recent study prepared by the Balkan Civil Society Development Network with the title "The missing Lens: Rethinking the Enabling Environment for Gender Equality and Civil Society in the Western Balkans 2025" alerts that despite formal legal guarantees for association, assembly, and expression, organizations operating in the field of gender equality face distinct structural, political, and societal challenges that diverge significantly from those encountered by the broader civil society sector. "The operational landscape for feminist and LGBTIQ organizations is marked by limited access to resources, bureaucratic obstacles, and a climate of increasing anti-gender narratives. While legal rights formally protect freedoms of assembly and expression, implementation remains inconsistent, with gender-focused demonstrations and advocacy efforts often met with opposition from conservative and nationalist groups in both physical and digital spaces. Online harassment, disinformation campaigns, and smear tactics have become normalized, posing significant risks for activists and organizations."
In the above context, Kvinna till kvinna and its partner organizations have significantly contributed to holding the border line through providing support to local women activists and women CSO's for their continued active functioning in the field.
Moreover, coordinated efforts by the supported local CSO's are done through the Gender Equality Platform together with other organizations supported by other Kvinna till kvinna implemented projects, in preparing Shadow reports on the Implementation of the Council of Europe Convention on Preventing and Combating Violence against Women and Domestic Violence in North Macedonia.
Further, the combined efforts by the supported Women CSO's with other organizations supported through other projects, contributed to introducing the gender equality recommendation in the EU Progress report for North Macedonia.
In the described challenging context the specific operations supported by this project made significant difference by holding the border line and even pushing for progress in gender equality and protection of human rights focusing on the needs of marginalized communities. The results achieved address the needs of most vulnerable groups including the rights of victims of GBV and DV; rural women; women textile workers, Roma women and women/people with disabilities.
Some of the achieved results have already achieved sustainability during the project implementation period (like allocation of municipal funding for counselling centers for women victims of GBV (Kavadarci, Bitola and Tetovo).
Unexpected project result was a specific case which have set the base to combat gender based discrimination for women employment in the country which is the first officially confirmed case of gender-based/pregnancy based discrimination in the country. This case is setting an important precedent and encouraging other women to come forward and report violations.
The established Womens Circle networks, currently spanning 64 villages across 21 municipalities, with more than 500 women actively engaged, continuously progressed in active advocacy to the local authorities for rural women rights and needs, even during the current phase of supported project, these women for the first time have been received by the Parliament and were able to present their needs in the rural areas.
Based on the above and many other results and initiated processes under the project which are continuing beyond the end of implementation of the project, Sida assesses that the project has achieved significant results in a very difficult context.
